## Code

```python
import numpy as np
x = np.linspace(0, 1, 5)   # a comment
print(x)
```

Inline code like `curve_fit` sits in prose.

A dollar sign inside a code block is text, not math:

```python
ax.set_xlabel("$V$ (V)")   # matplotlib reads the $...$ itself
```

## Math

Inline $E = h\nu$ and display:

$$ I(x) = \frac{I_0}{2}\left[1 - \operatorname{erf}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}\,x}{w}\right)\right] $$ {#eq-knife}

@eq-knife is the knife-edge model.

An unlabeled display equation carries no number:

$$ E = m c^2 $$

An aligned derivation spans lines:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P &= I V \\
  &= I^2 R
\end{aligned}
$$

A boxed result:

$$ \boxed{F = m a} $$
